devdoc.details: Why this exists (the bootstrap problem): the MintingHub charges OPENING_FEE = 1,000 units in currency to open the first position, `suggestMinter` costs >= 1,000 units, and the first Equity deposit needs >= 1,000 units — but at genesis supply is 0 and nobody owns any units (Frankencoin/OFD solved this with a source-stablecoin bridge registered at genesis; DogeOS has no dollar rail, so the bridge role is played by this allocation minter instead). Registered as a minter through the token's deployer-gated `initialize()` at genesis (the unavoidable bootstrap act — at supply 0 no veto is possible). Minter registrations are permanent (`denyMinter` reverts TooLate once active), so safety comes from inertness by construction: `execute()` mints the fixed genesis float exactly once and can never mint again. The float split (default 500k units per instance, see report/dogeos-tech-parts/03-collateral- monetary.md §3.2): pool seed (Barkswap pool), equity (treasury tranche-1 investment), challenger bounty, incentives. Recipients and amounts are immutable constructor parameters, so the only trust assumption is the deployer who registers the contract — the same trust domain as the genesis `initialize()` calls for Savings/PositionFactory/PositionRoller/MintingHub. If `execute()` never runs before `endTime`, the float is forfeited forever: with supply 0 the 1,000-unit fees can never be paid, so no other minter can ever be suggested. This makes endTime a hard deadline wired into the instance's genesis calendar.

execute().notice: Mint the genesis float once. Callable by anyone: recipients and amounts are immutable, so the caller has no influence over the outcome.
